title: Ab Externo Transconjunctival XEN® 45 Gel Stent Implantation: Efficacy and Safety of a New Surgical Technique

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article <license>: ali:license_ref and link point to by-nc/4.0 and the text permits non-commercial reproduction, although it names the 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License'); non-commercial or unclear, therefore private

indication: primary open-angle glaucoma with uncontrolled IOP, progression and/or intolerance of topical drugs; phakic eyes without previous glaucoma surgery or uveitis; XEN 45 gel stent implanted ab externo transconjunctivally with subtenon mitomycin C and a routine subconjunctival 5-fluorouracil injection 15 days after surgery; retrospective single-surgeon series, one eye per patient

groups.description: All eyes after ab externo transconjunctival XEN 45 implantation with mitomycin C (single-arm series; Table 1)

series.notes: mean ± SD; columns 'Baseline', '1 month', '2 months', '3 months', '6 months'; per-visit n not reported (all 31 eyes followed for at least 6 months); eyes that later needed bleb needling or revision are not stated to be removed

exclusions.what: 'Final mean IOP' in the Abstract and Results text
exclusions.reason: not a table cell; it corresponds to the 6-month column, which is cited

exclusions.what: Figures 2 and 3 (medications and IOP below 18 mmHg)
exclusions.reason: graphical medication data and success proportions are not admissible
examined according to Methods but not tabulated

notes: Reference: baseline IOP tabulated with the preoperative number of glaucoma medications (Results), recorded as preoperative_medicated.
Role: single-arm series of a technique the authors call new; no arm is declared experimental against a comparator, so the group is recorded as control.
Seven eyes required bleb needling and one of them a revision with a PreserFlo MicroShunt during follow-up (Results); no outcome-defined exclusion from the means is stated.
The Results text gives a different SD for the final mean IOP than the 6-month cell of Table 1; the table cell is cited.
The number of glaucoma medications is reported in the text and Figure 2 only; not extracted.
